# Summary {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| include: false
source(here::here("chapters", "_setup.R"))
by30 <- pain_by_group(clean, "pain_30min")
or30 <- odds_ratio(fit_single_timepoint(clean))
or_marginal <- odds_ratio(fit_marginal(long))
```

**Question.** Does gargling licorice before intubation reduce postoperative
sore throat compared with a sugar-water gargle?

**Answer.** Yes, in this trial. Thirty minutes after arrival in recovery,
`r fmt_pct(by30$proportion[by30$group == "Licorice"])` of licorice patients
reported any sore throat at rest, against
`r fmt_pct(by30$proportion[by30$group == "Sugar"])` of sugar-water patients
(`r fmt_or(or30)`; `r fmt_p(or30$p_value)`). Across all four assessments
through the first postoperative morning, the population-averaged odds of sore
throat were lower with licorice (`r fmt_or(or_marginal)`).

**How to read this book.** It is both the lab notebook and the report. The
*Plan* part was written before the results; the *Results* part follows it;
the *Record* part holds every analysis decision and the research log. Every
number in the prose is computed from the data when the book renders, so the
text cannot drift from the analysis.

::: {.callout-note}
## This is a teaching example
The data are the public licorice gargle trial (Ruetzler et al., *Anesth
Analg* 2013), distributed in the `medicaldata` R package. The "client" and
the engagement are fictional; the analysis is real.
:::
